queue.brief: The town is empty after dark, so #51's going-home mechanism fires under once a night. Give the night its own arrival source: `spawnHomeAgent()` sends a walker in from a lane edge after `nightF > 0.3` who walks straight to an unused `HOME_DOORS` entry whose `windowHours()` says somebody is home tonight and whose priced `pathHours()` arrival fits before `HOME_MIN` of the dawn edge, then goes in through `arriveHome()` so the window over that door lights the frame they enter. Model it on `spawnTapAgent`: its own rate and its own presence bound (at most two on the way at once), excluded from the count `scarcity` reads, never a share of `laneCap`. Also fix c87 while you are in `drawFaceRow`: a row-64 pane over a home door is drawn live and then night-tinted, so it lands at half the warmth of a cached pane — a window someone just came home to must read as warm as the rest.
queue.successLooksLike: Over ten seed-nights `probes/going-home.mjs` counts 3–5 arrivals a night (from under 1), every one inside its window's hours, and `windows-night.mjs` total lit counts stay within noise of HEAD because the register only moves WHEN a window lights, not whether. A midnight wide shot shows a figure on the lane walking toward a door; the pane over it goes from dark to full warmth the frame they vanish.
queue.avoid: Do not widen laneCap or let these walkers take lane itineraries — they are going home, one leg, no stops. Do not change windowHours()'s hash or the 0.15–2 h dusk offsets; the register is the only thing that moves. Expect census churn from the new R() draws: replay over ten seeds, read for collapse only.

queue.brief: The wind now reaches the fountain and stops there. The river is the largest surface in the picture and reads the same on a gale as on a still day: `drawRiverFlow()` draws FLOW_N streaks off `riverRun()` alone, `drawRiverLights()` breaks its lamp and moon columns on a fixed chop, and `updateBoat`/`boatRate()` row the same in any weather. Make a windy day legible on the water from the east wide shot — more, shorter, crosswise-slanted streaks and a rougher chop on the reflections when `windF()` is 1, the rowboat rarer and slower into the wind — with every term exact at `windF() = 0` so the calm day and the anchor are byte-identical. Take c78 with it: the rowboat has no reflection after dark and the bridge deck casts no shadow on the water; add both only if they fall out of the same pass.
